entries.en: We sent in a team as you instructed. Kyle's followers have disbanded, and the major surrendered to us without incident. We'll make sure he gets the help he needs.
To be honest, Shepard, I thought this thing was going to end in a bloodbath. I don't know how you did it, but you saved a lot of lives. Congratulations.
What kind of proof do you have that the major is dangerous?
What else can you tell me about Major Kyle?
You said his followers were biotics?
What were those Alliance representatives going to talk to Major Kyle about?
I'll deal with Major Kyle for you, Admiral.
I might be able to end this without violence.
How permanent of a solution are you looking for?
Maybe you're overreacting.
Okay.
Kyle's Followers
Missing Alliance Officers
I'll look into this.
Maybe I can reason with him.
You want me to kill him?
I've received some information I thought you'd want to see, Commander.
I've received some troubling information, Commander. We need your help.
Someone is killing former Alliance scientists. There have been four deaths in the past month.
We found a connection between the scientists... and you.
They all worked on a classified project several years ago. On Akuze.
I can't get any information on what they were working on. The project records are sealed.
Those thresher maws killed dozens of soldiers. If this was more than just an accident, we need to know.
Commander... Shepard. What you do with this is up to you. I just thought you'd want to know.
All four scientists worked on a classified project on Akuze.
There was a brutal massacre there years ago. An entire unit was killed by thresher maws.
It was classified as a natural hazard, but the project dates coincide with the attacks.
I'm not certain what I think. But it's worth investigating.
There was one other scientist on the project: Dr. Wayne. I'm transmitting his last known coordinates. Good luck. Fifth Fleet out.
Understood, Commander. Sorry to trouble you. Fifth Fleet out.
Former scientists? Sounds like someone has a project they'd like to keep secret.
I'm happy to look into it, Admiral. What can you tell me?
Akuze... I lost my whole unit there. You're saying that our scientists were involved?
This can't have anything to do with what happened to me on Akuze.
You think these scientists had something to do with the attack?
That can't be a coincidence.
I've got higher priorities than retired scientists, Admiral. Find someone else.
Sounds like a cover up.
What did they work on?
Those bastards.
The site of the massacre.
It must be a coincidence.
They were involved.
That sounds suspicious.
I reviewed your report of the situation, Commander.
You did well to save the doctor. I suppose we'll never know what set Toombs off.
It's unfortunate both the doctor and Toombs died, but I know you did your best under the circumstances.
It's unfortunate Dr. Wayne ended up dead. But based on your report, your actions were understandable.
I'm glad you were able to take Dr. Wayne in alive. Now we can put him on trial and get some answers.
I just wish we could have saved Corporal Toombs, too.
Corporal Toombs seems to have found some closure. Hopefully, with therapy, he'll have a normal life again someday.
I hope this helped you find some peace, Commander. Thank you. Fifth Fleet out.
Thank you again for your assistance, Commander. Fifth Fleet out.
Commander, incoming signal from Fifth Fleet HQ on the Citadel.
Commander Shepard. Something uncomfortable has just come up.
In the First Contact War, we fired a lot of espionage probes into turian space. We've just received a "mission complete" burst from one of them.
No idea. Lost in transit. These probes were built in a hurry after first contact.
When these probes were launched, we didn't have any idea who we were fighting. We didn't want to risk aliens examining our technology.
The probe has a demo nuke built in. A 20-kiloton tactical fusion warhead. About equal to the bomb dropped on Hiroshima back in the 20th.
If somebody finds that probe, tampers with it-- you don't need me to finish, Commander.
I know. I wouldn't ask if it wasn't important. These probes have been classified for 26 years.
The Council would call fusion-bomb booby traps "dangerous and irresponsible." The Alliance would face censure if they find this probe.
I'm asking you because the Normandy can get on-site quickly and quietly. It's in the Voyager Cluster.
I don't know. It's possible someone recovered it safely and brought it there.
It's also possible it got very badly lost. It could have been wandering the relay network since the war.
All right. I'll see if I can find someone else to handle this.
I appreciate that, Commander. Good luck.
Fifth Fleet out.
What makes this "uncomfortable?"
Where's it been in the meantime?
And this is a problem... why?
The war's over. What difference does it make?
I understand this must be handled. But I don't have anyone trained to deal with this sort of thing, sir.
Just because I saved Eden Prime doesn't make me an expert on nuclear munitions.
Shouldn't a bomb disposal unit be sent for this? We don't have anyone trained in that.
It's in the Voyager Cluster? That's the opposite side of the Alliance from turian space. How did it get there?
By the time we finish our current objectives, you could have someone else on-site.
We'll get on it immediately, Admiral. And we'll be discreet.
Straightforward enough.
That's quite a delay.
It shouldn't matter.
That's serious all right.
Get a bomb disposal team.
We'll handle it.
It shouldn't be over there.
We're busy.
Where is it?
Commander - I'm picking up a signal from the planet's surface. Looks like an automated distress beacon.
Message for you, Commander. Just came in over a secure channel.
Shepard, this is Admiral Kahoku. I found out who set that trap for my men. The ones killed by the thresher maw.
Damn, I hope you get this message.
It was a group called Cerberus. An Alliance black ops organization. Top secret, highest-level security clearance.
They vanished a few months ago. Dropped right off the grid. Nobody knew where they went or what they were up to.
They've gone completely rogue, Shepard. They're conducting illegal genetic experiments, trying to create some kind of super soldier.
I don't have any proof, but I found the coordinates for one of their research worlds. I'm uploading them with this message.
They're completely out of control. Somebody needs to stop them. I've done my part. Now, it's up to you.
This is... this is probably the last you'll hear from me. Cerberus is after me now. I need to disappear before they find me.
Transmission coming in, Commander. I think you're going to want to hear this one.
Greetings, Commander Shepard. I represent a party interested in obtaining information on Cerberus activities.
Who I am is inconsequential. Suffice to say, I am an agent for the Shadow Broker.
I suspect I know less about Cerberus than you do. I am merely an agent for the Shadow Broker.
You see, Admiral Kahoku contacted my employer looking for information on the location of any Cerberus facilities.
We provided that information on the promise that he would turn over copies of all files gathered from the Cerberus systems to us.
Information is our business, Commander. Through our contacts, we were able to determine that the Cerberus group was active in the Voyager cluster.
Unfortunately, that was all we were able to find out. That is why we are so interested in acquiring copies of the files from you.
We had no reason to harm him. He was going to provide us with information about Cerberus. Information that is now in your possession.
Be reasonable, Commander. Cerberus was operating outside Alliance jurisdiction. You don't owe them any loyalty.
The Alliance is just going to file this information away in some archive. But no secret stays hidden forever. Eventually, someone somewhere will deliver it into our hands.
It might as well be you. Transmit the files to us and you will be well compensated.
Information is a commodity. It can be bought, sold, or traded. Why my employer desires this information is not my concern. I am only the buyer.
That is unfortunate, Commander. My employer will remember this the next time you need something from us.
I knew you were a reasonable woman, Commander. My employer will remember this the next time you need something from us.
I knew you were a reasonable man, Commander. My employer will remember this the next time you need something from us.
Who are you? And who do you represent?
If you know something about Cerberus, you'd better tell me.
You must have some connection to Cerberus. How else could you tell Kahoku where to find them?
Did you have anything to do with Admiral Kahoku ending up dead?
These are classified Alliance files. I'm not handing them over to you.
Your deal died with Kahoku. Why should I help you?
What are you going to do with this information?
My loyalty is to the Alliance, not the Shadow Broker.
I'll transmit the files.
What's your name?
Cut to the chase.
Facility location
Kahoku's death
That's treason!
Why do you want the files?
I don't trust you.
Commander, I'm glad you were in the area.
We've got an emergency situation, and you're the only one I trust to get the job done.
How can I help, Admiral?
I'm sorry, Admiral. I've got too much going on right now to help.
I can't.
I didn't think it could be done, Commander.
You managed to secure the base and neutralize the biotics without a single civilian casualty.
I wish every soldier had your definition of "just doing your job".
They certainly will.
You're a credit to the uniform, Shepard. We're in your debt. Fifth Fleet out.
Good work, Commander. You took down the biotics with minimal collateral damage.
The biotics had every advantage, including human shields.
You lost a handful of civilians. Any other unit I sent in would have lost dozens of innocent lives.
Nobody could have gotten out of there with fewer innocent lives lost.
You saved a lot of lives today, Commander. Fifth Fleet out.
What the hell happened out there, Commander? I brought you in to avoid a bloodbath!
You've been in tighter spots than that. There's always a choice.
You're not being charged with anything. Neutralizing the biotics was the top priority.
I had hoped for fewer casualties, but on paper, this mission is still a success.
Your assistance in this matter is noted, Commander. Fifth Fleet out.
Damn it! I'm not asking you because it's convenient! Nobody else can get this done.
